summary: Clinic facials used to support skin cleansing, exfoliation and general skin quality.
leadAnswer: Facial Treatments at Kaiteki are clinic-based facials, including Hydrafacial and Silkpeel, that combine cleansing, exfoliation and skin-conditioning steps to support general skin quality. They work at the surface rather than on deeper structural concerns, and a skin assessment decides which one suits you, or whether your skin needs medical treatment instead.

bringToConsult: Mention your skincare and medical history, especially any known sensitivity to skincare products.

An eczema or rosacea flare, or sunburn.
Straight after a peel, laser or waxing

avoidIf.body: which can mean waiting or adjusting the facial.

sessionSteps.title: Skin assessment
sessionSteps.body: Your first visit starts with an assessment, not a treatment. It confirms which facial suits you, or whether your skin needs medical treatment instead.

sessionSteps.title: The facial
sessionSteps.body: The skin is cleansed, exfoliated and, depending on the option, given device-based extraction and serum infusion. Sessions are generally comfortable, and most people return to normal activities straight away.

afterSession.intro: Mild, temporary redness can follow some facials and usually settles within a few hours. Uncommonly, a serum causes an irritation reaction. Use sun protection and gentle skincare afterwards.

bands.title: The next day or two
bands.body: Keep skincare gentle, and hold off on strong actives such as retinoids and acids unless advised otherwise.

risks.intro: Clinic facials are low-risk for most people, but not risk-free.
risks.common: Redness, mild sensitivity or tightness, and small areas of irritation where extraction was firm.
risks.lessCommon: A short-lived breakout as congestion clears, and, uncommonly, a reaction to a serum ingredient.
cannotDo: It works at the surface, not on deeper structural concerns.
It is not a substitute for medical treatment of acne or pigmentation.
Congestion tends to return without a suitable home routine, which is why a facial is maintenance rather than a one-off.
risks.disclose: Tell the clinician about your current products, any past reactions and any recent isotretinoin.

costFactors.intro: Cost depends on which facial is chosen and what is added to it, so it is confirmed once that is settled.
factors: Which facial is chosen, and the steps included.
Add-ons such as serum boosters, extractions, masking or LED.
Whether areas beyond the face are treated.
How often you choose to come in.

sections.heading: What are Facial Treatments?
body: Facial Treatments are clinic-based procedures that combine cleansing, exfoliation and skin-conditioning steps in a single session, generally with gentler technology than laser or energy-based devices. At Kaiteki this category includes Hydrafacial and Silkpeel.
They are typically considered for congested pores, dull or uneven-looking tone and general hydration, as routine maintenance or between other treatments.

sections.heading: How do Hydrafacial and Silkpeel work?
body: Hydrafacial uses a device-based process that cleanses, exfoliates and extracts debris from pores before infusing serums suited to the skin. Silkpeel combines exfoliation with simultaneous infusion of topical solutions.
Both aim to clear surface build-up, refine texture and support hydration rather than treat deeper structural concerns.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Hydrafacial and Silkpeel?
faqs.a: Both combine exfoliation with serum infusion, but they use different device technology and formulations. The clinician advises which suits your skin.

faqs.q: Can facials replace treatments like Pico laser or skin boosters?
faqs.a: No. Facials address surface skin quality; lasers and injectables work at a different level, for more specific concerns. A facial can sit alongside them in a wider plan.

faqs.q: How often should I get a facial?
faqs.a: There is no single frequency that suits everyone. Facials are booked periodically as maintenance, at an interval set by your skin and goals.

faqs.q: Is a clinic facial suitable for sensitive skin?
faqs.a: Often yes, because suction, exfoliation and solutions can all be turned down, and no light or laser energy is involved. It is deferred during an eczema or rosacea flare, over broken skin, or soon after a peel, laser or waxing.

faqs.q: Can a facial clear blackheads and clogged pores?
faqs.a: Extraction after exfoliation is commonly used for congestion and blackheads, but congestion tends to return without a suitable home routine. If it is really inflammatory acne, the doctor may recommend medical treatment instead.
